candidates.name: Local ordinary discriminants at odd roots of unity
candidates.plainmeaning: Describes exactly how repeated Rogers–Szegő roots split when q moves away from a fixed root of unity, including the extra collision at −1, and computes the first nonzero ordinary discriminant coefficient.
exactclaim: Let H_n(z;q)=sum_k [n choose k]_q z^k, D_n(q)=Disc_z H_n, n=Ad+b, d odd, ω primitive of order d, and q(ε)=ω(1+ε²)^(1/d). Put F=z^d+1 and P_A=product_(j=1)^A j^j.

Separated case: G=H_b(z;ω), 0≤b<d, A≥1, Disc(G)Res(F,G)≠0. At α^d=−1, H_n(α+εx;q(ε))=ε^A(−1)^A d^(A/2)G(α)He_A(√d x/α)+O(ε^(A+1)). With K=dA(A−1)/2, D_n(q(ε))=ε^(2K)(C+O(ε²)), C=(−1)^(A(d−1)/2)d^(dA(A+1)/2)P_A^d Disc(G)Res(F,G)^(2A). Thus ord_(Φ_d)D_n=K.

Simple-overlap case: d≥3, b odd with 1≤b<d. Write G=(z+1)U, g=U(−1), W=(ω;ω)_b/(ω²;ω²)_((b+d)/2), τ=dW/g and J_(A+1)=He_(A+1)+A(1−τ)He_(A−1). If g≠0, H_n(−1+εx;q(ε))=ε^(A+1)(−1)^(A+1)d^((A−1)/2)g J_(A+1)(−√d x;τ)+O(ε^(A+2)).

If additionally Disc(U)Res(F,U)Disc(J_(A+1))≠0, L=dA(A−1)/2+A and D_n(q(ε))=ε^(2L)(C+O(ε²)), C=(−1)^(A(d−1)/2)d^(dA(A+1)/2+A)P_A^(d−1)Disc(J_(A+1))Disc(U)Res(F,U)^(2A)g². Hence ord_(Φ_d)D_n=L. Square roots cancel coefficientwise.
candidates.model: Characteristic-zero formal series; ordinary z-derivative discriminant; arbitrary fixed odd d with the stated residual guards. Disc(1)=1.
candidates.proofstatus: Both separated and overlap theorems were accepted in saved independent audits. This catalogue re-read the proofs and qualifications, but did not repeat their computations or create a fresh independent correctness audit.
candidates.noveltystatus: Plausible specific theorem package; external priority remains unresolved. Standard q-Lucas, Hermite limits, quasi-Laguerre discriminants and hook-Wronskian theory are not new.
candidates.whatnew: The narrow candidate is the explicitly normalized fixed-nontrivial-ω, moving-z local coefficient, especially τ and the shared-root coefficient, together with its full ordinary discriminant and arithmetic use.
candidates.limits: Only separated or exactly one simple shared residual root at −1. Nonzero residual discriminant/resultant and Disc J are essential. No arbitrary-overlap, repeated-p, all-composite, or globally cleared novelty theorem.
candidates.publicationreadiness: Best algebra manuscript-development core; needs self-contained exposition and legitimate full-text priority comparisons, especially Lubinsky–Saff 1987 and Zhedanov 1997. No originality announcement warranted.
candidates.rationale: Ranks first in this domain: uniform exact formulas with independent proof audits, coherent special-functions/arithmetic consequences, and a more visible substantive increment than isolated certificate or standard-ingredient applications.

candidates.name: Nonzero one-window common-chirp phase eliminant
candidates.plainmeaning: Turns an unknown common quadratic phase into a bounded list of algebraic candidates from one short data window.
exactclaim: For r≥1, N≥3r, F_p containing supplied ω of exact order N, a nonzero x_j=ω^(aj²)sum_(ℓ=1)^s c_ℓω^(b_ℓj), s≤r, has a nonzero center c in [r,N−r−1]. Put h=c−r.

P_h(t)=t^(−E)det[x_(h+i+j)t^binom(i+j,2)]_(i,j=0)^r is a polynomial, E=(r+1)r(r−1)/2. It has degree at most D=binom(r+2,3), constant coefficient (−1)^(r(r+1)/2)x_c^(r+1)≠0, and P_h(ω^(−2a))=0 for every valid phase.

There are at most min(D,N/gcd(2,N)) canonical phase candidates. For even N phases a and a+N/2 are equivalent after frequency translation. The all-zero input is rank-zero and must be handled separately.
candidates.model: Exact finite-field root-of-unity grid, bounded common chirp rank; N≥3r is a witness guarantee, not a universal identifiability threshold.
candidates.proofstatus: Accepted independent audit of the full recognition theorem; polynomial proof uses unique extremal determinant terms, not fitted degrees. Catalogue has inspected theorem/audit text; no source program executed.
candidates.noveltystatus: Specific certificate may be original; not cleared. Common-rate chirps, dechirping and Hankel/Prony are established.
candidates.whatnew: A uniformly bounded, provably nonzero window polynomial and complete exact finite-grid candidate reduction. Algorithms worker owns the O_r(N) recognizer and polynomial Toeplitz/Bareiss construction costs.
candidates.limits: Degree is an upper bound and can drop. Vanishing supplies candidates, not membership; full-input verification is essential. No representation uniqueness, robust floating-point recovery, or arbitrary-input fast DFT.
candidates.publicationreadiness: Good secondary algorithm/algebra note candidate after broader algebraic chirp-identification comparison; strongest in combination with charged exact recognition.
candidates.rationale: Ranks above the reciprocal-pencil formula because the nonzero witness gives a concrete all-input recognition mechanism and avoids degeneracy-based completeness gaps, while retaining limited fixed-r structured-input scope.

candidates.name: Universal reciprocal diagonal-pencil resultant
candidates.plainmeaning: Extracts universal factors and reciprocal symmetry from a family of determinant resultants, substantially reducing interpolation degree.
exactclaim: For arbitrary m×m A,B over a commutative ring, D(w)=diag(1,w,...,w^(m−1)), P0=det(A−aDAD), P1=det(B−awDBD), and R=Res_a(P0,P1) with fixed degree-m homogeneous Sylvester convention, set T=m²(2m−1), v=m(m−1)(4m+1)/6 and b=m(m−1)(2m−1)/6.
w^T R(1/w)=(−1)^(m²)R(w); R=w^v(w−1)^(m²)U; w^(2b)U(1/w)=U(w); U=w^bV(w+w^(−1)) with deg V≤b.

The accepted adjacent-Hankel theorem is A_ij=T_(i+j), B_ij=T_(i+j+1), m=s+1. Universal identities survive singular, leading-coefficient-drop, and zero-resultant specializations. Generic w=0 valuation is exact; specialization may raise it.
candidates.model: Integral polynomial identities under fixed formal degree. General arbitrary-matrix extension has an assessment-level proof; Hankel specialization has a separate accepted audit.
candidates.proofstatus: Adjacent-Hankel theorem accepted by Phase21 independent audit. General-pencil extension is a checked direct derivation in a publication assessment, expressly not a separate independently accepted audit package.
candidates.noveltystatus: Possibly original printed formula/application; proof mechanisms standard. Later generalization demotes a uniquely Hankel or broad-new-elimination interpretation, not the theorem correctness.
candidates.whatnew: Closed all-m exponents, integral specialization, and compressed sparse-rational recovery application. At m=5/s=4, core interpolation uses 31 values rather than conservative 226; executable adds three witnesses.
candidates.limits: Cannot call factors exact after every specialization; cannot infer candidate sufficiency from zero homogeneous resultant. Sparse recovery requires nonzero probes/resultant, linear gcd and global invertibility/cyclic certification. Old benchmark counters and executable domain are separately qualified.
candidates.publicationreadiness: Useful specialized theorem or methods note; modest standalone significance absent stronger recovery/generalization beyond standard determinant/Newton facts.
candidates.rationale: Ranks third: universal and audited, but later arbitrary-pencil derivation shows a short specialization of established machinery and reduces its independent conceptual increment.

candidates.name: Exact legal scalar chirp-resolvent bank minima
candidates.plainmeaning: Determines the fewest first-order resolvents of one fixed cycle needed to synthesize an odd quadratic chirp, and how one free diagonal changes that answer.
exactclaim: For N=2m+1≥3, primitive q in characteristic zero, h=(N+1)/2, f(k)=q^(hk²), C=sum_(k=0)^(N−1)f(k)P^k, represent C=sum_(s=1)^Q a_s(I−λ_sP)^(−1), with a_s,λ_s≠0 and λ_s^N≠1. Without a free diagonal Qmin=m+1 for every odd N.
With δI free, Qmin=m iff T_m(z)=(-1)^mH_m(−z;q) has simple nonzero nonresonant roots; otherwise Qmin=m+1. An arbitrary free diagonal does not enlarge this scalar common-P circulant model.
T_m(0)=(-1)^m. gcd(T_m,z^N−1)=1 for N≡1 mod4 and z−1 for N≡3 mod4, the latter root simple. Thus all N≡3 mod4 have Qmin=m+1. Every prime N≡1 mod4 and the audited infinite families have Qmin=m.
When Qmin=m, δ=(-1)^m q^(−m(m+1)/2)product_(j=1)^m(1−q^j) is forced and nonzero. Nodes/weights may lie in an algebraic closure; root-free sum works over Q(q).
candidates.model: Scalar coefficients, same natural cycle P, first-order nonconfluent resolvents, no branch-dependent diagonal endpoints or independent routing.
candidates.proofstatus: Uniform construction/minimum and partial free-diagonal classification independently accepted. Nonsingular Hankel lower bound and guarded polynomial-pencil upper construction both checked.
candidates.noveltystatus: Specific exact legal-bank classification potentially new as an application; finite-moment/Prony/Padé/formal-orthogonality ingredients classical. External novelty unconfirmed.
candidates.whatnew: Exact legal-node count in this fixed grammar, uniform resonance classification, forced diagonal and explicit root-free construction. This is distinct from the five-coordinate all-order Green exact-three theorem.
candidates.limits: No unrestricted inverse-bank minimum or all-composite squarefreeness. Branch nodes not necessarily in Q(q). O(N³) setup/O(N²) application generally, improved O(N²) setup on lower-bank cases, exact field operations only.
candidates.publicationreadiness: Substantive restricted-model theorem, best application/companion section to RS work or Green realization note; broad standalone significance less clear.
candidates.rationale: Ranks fourth: a genuine exact minimum with strong proofs, but its grammar is narrow and core moment mechanisms old; the unresolved general composite guard precludes a full closed-form classification.

candidates.name: All-anchor primitive-holonomy curvature obstruction
candidates.plainmeaning: Shows that a single cycle Green kernel has an invariant exponent geometry incompatible with Fourier, independent of all row/column anchors and relabelings.
candidates.exactclaim: For N=2^m≥4 and legal cycle G=(I−αW)^(−1) with α^N=ω^c primitive of order N, every (N−1)×(N−1) anchored exponent-curvature matrix has determinant a unit mod N and rank N−1 over F2. Fourier anchored exponent curvature is an outer product and has F2 rank one. Hence no invertible outer diagonal scalings and independent permutations make these kernels Fourier-equivalent.
candidates.model: Dyadic N, primitive holonomy c coprime to N, nonzero-entry legal single-cycle kernel; exponents are in Z/NZ, F2 is the derived exponent field.
candidates.proofstatus: Accepted independent Phase37 proof audit; all-anchor step uses unimodular bases of the zero-sum lattice. Independent finite controls support rather than establish the uniform theorem.
candidates.noveltystatus: Specific anchored determinant deduction is a possible specialized result; underlying four-entry curvature invariant is classical Haagerup-type material. No standalone novelty priority established.
candidates.whatnew: The explicit full-rank all-anchor holonomy calculation and direct projective obstruction, not a new cross-ratio invariant.
candidates.limits: Primitive-holonomy hypothesis matters; no freely varying sum/product or all-cycle-bank exclusion. Ratios must lie in the root subgroup before exponent-parity extraction.
candidates.publicationreadiness: Useful lemma or certification-methods appendix; weak standalone publication priority.
candidates.rationale: Ranks fifth: uniform and clean, but specialized model and classical invariant leave a modest substantive novelty increment.

candidates.name: Reciprocal-parameter paired squarefreeness
candidates.plainmeaning: Uses two conjugate residue components to guarantee that at least one shared-root splitting polynomial remains simple.
exactclaim: For d≡3 mod4, b=(d−1)/2, the overlap parameters at ω and ω^(−1) satisfy 1/τ+1/τ*=1 where defined; a denominator-free identity also holds.
For prime p≡3 mod4, A=(p−1)/2, at least one of J_(A+1)(y;τ), J_(A+1)(y;τ*) is squarefree when the reciprocal relation and nonzero-parameter guards hold.

Let U_b=H_b/(z+1), Γ_d=Disc(U_b)Res(z^d+1,U_b), and c_d^pair be the coefficient content of the nonzero canonical remainder Γ_d(q)Γ_d(q^(d−1)) mod Φ_d. If p∤d c_d^pair, H_((dp−1)/2)(z;ζ_dp) is squarefree.
candidates.model: Distinct paired-content invariant; ordinary derivatives, p≡3 mod4, p∤d, one good residue component suffices.
candidates.proofstatus: Accepted in overlap independent audit.
candidates.noveltystatus: Specific reciprocal pairing/application candidate; standalone Wronskian ingredient is an exact known hook specialization.
candidates.whatnew: The coupling of inverse residue factors to the local RS ramified bridge.
candidates.limits: p≡1 mod4 can have a zero-root obstruction; cannot assert all residue components good or apply at p|d.
candidates.publicationreadiness: Corollary/section of ALG-RS-LOCAL, not another independent paper claim.
candidates.rationale: Uniform arithmetic consequence strengthens the main package; dependent on its local coefficient and standard ingredients.

candidates.name: Eleven fixed-base ramified squarefreeness families
candidates.plainmeaning: Converts exact lower-order computations into infinitely many characteristic-zero squarefreeness results.
exactclaim: Separated bases d∈{5,9,13,17,21,25}: H_((dp−1)/2)(z;ζ_dp) is squarefree for every odd prime p∤d. c_d^sep equals 5, 3^8, 13^4, 17^6, 3^11·7^9, 5^17 respectively.
Overlap bases d∈{3,7,11,15,19}: squarefreeness for every prime p≡3 mod4 with p∤d. Paired contents are 1, 7², 11^5, 3^12·5^9, 19^11 respectively.

Existing individually accepted certificates supply N=25,169 for the initial separated p≡1 mod4 families, and N=9,45,49,121,361 for all excluded p|d cases in the five overlap p≡3 mod4 families. The new separated bases alone do not supply N=289,63,147,125.
candidates.model: Infinite prime-index families are proved by uniform theorem plus finite fixed-base inputs. The eleven parameterizations can overlap; not eleven independent discoveries.
candidates.proofstatus: Independent audits verify the uniform arguments and full fixed-base coefficient arrays; finite exceptional target certificates separately reconstructed.
candidates.noveltystatus: New within project; external novelty unresolved and inherited classical zero theory still needs complete comparison.
candidates.whatnew: Replaces finite target census with genuine infinitely many composite orders and exact scalar-bank minima where N≡1 mod4.
candidates.limits: No all odd composites, arbitrary prime powers, or all 5r². Congruence and p∤d guards cannot be silently dropped.
candidates.publicationreadiness: Substantial consequences within the same local-discriminant manuscript; finite arrays belong in supporting data.
candidates.rationale: Infinite quantification is real, but all rows share mechanisms and must not inflate manuscript count.

candidates.name: Conditional exact ramified coefficient-content valuation
candidates.plainmeaning: Computes exactly how much a new prime divides every coefficient of the lower discriminant-resultant obstruction.
candidates.exactclaim: Define c_d^sep as content of nonzero rem_(Φ_d)(D_((d−1)/2)(q)Res_z(z^d+1,H_((d−1)/2)(z;q))), with c_1^sep=1. If s>0, s≡1 mod4, p≡1 mod4 prime, c_s^sep≠0 and p∤s c_s^sep, then c_(sp)^sep≠0 and v_p(c_(sp)^sep)=floor(3s(p−1)/8). In particular v_ℓ(c_ℓ^sep)=floor(3(ℓ−1)/8) for primes ℓ≡1 mod4.
candidates.model: Rational coefficient content, hence minimum valuation over all primes above p, not a norm. Whole integer cyclotomic division precedes reduction.
candidates.proofstatus: Accepted independent content audit; proof supplies lower valuation at every upper prime and equality at one explicitly selected good upper prime.
candidates.noveltystatus: Clean specific application candidate; terminal minimum/floor step and cyclotomic ramification classical.
candidates.whatnew: The exact application exponent coming from local product order L=3s((p−1)/2)²/2.
candidates.limits: No repeated-p ramification, p≡3 mod4 analogue, or determination of unramified prime support.
candidates.publicationreadiness: Good arithmetic corollary in ALG-RS-LOCAL, not a claimed new general ramification theory.
candidates.rationale: Uniform exact number-theoretic formula adds substance, but depends on local splitting and conventional arithmetic.

candidates.name: Reciprocal contraction of the unramified obstruction
candidates.plainmeaning: Reduces a large Gaussian-polynomial content question to a smaller multiplication determinant.
candidates.exactclaim: For d=4r+1≥5, H_(2r)(z;ζ_d)=z^rP(z+z^(−1)), η_j=−ζ_d^j−ζ_d^(−j), C_d*=product_(j=2)^(2r−1)(u−η_j), and M_d=Res_u(P,(u−2)P′C_d*). For p∤d, p|c_d^sep iff M_d∈pZ[ζ_d]. Also Disc H=P(2)P(−2)(Disc P)² and D_(2r)R_d=(−1)^rH(1)[H(−1)Disc(P)Res(C_d,P)]².
candidates.model: Canonical cyclotomic power basis; componentwise vanishing, including characteristic two. Empty product at d=5 allowed.
candidates.proofstatus: Accepted independent audit with full signs and finite arrays checked.
candidates.noveltystatus: Useful specialized reduction built from standard reciprocal-polynomial and resultant identities; no cleared independent novelty.
candidates.whatnew: Removes two known unit factors and halves the relevant polynomial degree for the actual Gaussian obstruction.
candidates.limits: Only an equivalent smaller obstruction, not proof it never vanishes. Reduced determinant content has different ramified exponents than c_d^sep.
candidates.publicationreadiness: Supporting lemma and computational tool.
candidates.rationale: Valuable for a proof strategy, insufficient alone for uniform support.

candidates.name: Explicit Galois-orbit content certificate

An explicit trace-dual construction gives W∈O with sum_aσ_a(W)σ_a(M)=dc. Consequently a certificate with right side d^L exists iff c has no prime divisor outside d.

candidates.name: Countercontrols for overly weak primitivity strategies
candidates.plainmeaning: Identifies precise ways natural proof strategies can fail without disproving the desired target theorem.
exactclaim: At actual d=17,p=2, the bad degree-eight residue factor of M_17 is preserved by subgroup <2>={1,2,4,8,9,13,15,16}, which contains conjugation; a conjugate outside it removes that obstruction. Another good factor remains, so 2∤c_17.

For every d=4r+1≥25 and odd p∤d, there exists a different monic degree-r polynomial Ptilde preserving the actual P values at 2,−2,η_1,η_(2r), but with u²|Ptilde modulo p. Thus four special values plus reciprocity cannot force the desired nonvanishing.
Norm(R_17)=2^16·17^68·101^4 although 2∤c_17: norm divisibility is not coefficient-content divisibility.
candidates.model: One exact actual subgroup obstruction plus a uniform synthetic, non-Gaussian perturbation theorem.
candidates.proofstatus: Saved parent proof review and fresh controls, not separate full independent audit.
candidates.noveltystatus: Useful strategy obstructions, external novelty not established; synthetic result is elementary interpolation/perturbation.
candidates.whatnew: Prevents false strengthening from subgroup conjugates, norms or Gaussian special values alone.
candidates.limits: Not a target counterexample. Ptilde does not preserve the full q-Pascal/three-term Gaussian recurrence.
candidates.publicationreadiness: Keep as a caveat/proof-strategy appendix, unranked.
candidates.rationale: Important negative evidence for correctness discipline, modest standalone significance.

candidates.name: Characteristic-two squarefreeness reduction
candidates.plainmeaning: Expresses the ordinary discriminant of a reciprocal Rogers–Szegő polynomial through a smaller parity resultant.
candidates.exactclaim: Over F2[q], H_(2r)(z)=z^rP_r(z+z^(−1)), P_r(0)=product_(j=1)^r(1+q^(2j−1)), and for P_r(y)=A_r(y²)+yB_r(y²), Disc H_(2r)=P_r(0)²Res(A_r,B_r)^4. For N=4r+1 and exact-order q in a characteristic-two field, H_(2r) squarefree iff Res(A_r,B_r)(q)≠0. Equivalently Φ_N does not divide that resultant iff at least one primitive residue factor is good.
candidates.model: Ordinary formal derivative in characteristic two; field exact-order hypotheses essential, quotient by Φ_N may have zero divisors.
candidates.proofstatus: All identities and logical equivalences independently accepted; only reduction, not uniform target nonvanishing.
candidates.noveltystatus: Classical reciprocal/discriminant mechanisms applied to Gaussian recurrence; no established standalone novelty.
candidates.whatnew: Concrete smaller sufficient nonvanishing target and explicit diagonal reduction δ=q^(16^(−1) mod N) for odd N≥3.
candidates.limits: No inference from Φ_N nondivisibility to gcd(Φ_N,R)=1. Field construction/factor search charged separately; no all-composite proof.
candidates.publicationreadiness: Supporting reduction and failure-boundary record.
candidates.rationale: Preserve as mathematics; do not rank a remaining conjectural target as proved.

candidates.name: Classical inputs and exact antecedent reductions
candidates.plainmeaning: Separates reused theory from the genuinely specific candidate theorem.
exactclaim: Root-of-unity q-Lucas factorization H_(Ad+b)(z;ω)=(1+z^d)^AH_b(z;ω) is known; continuous q-Hermite equivalent explicitly appears as equation (2.8) of Atakishiyeva–Atakishiyev–Koornwinder.
General q→1 Hermite degeneration and Disc He_A=product j^j are classical. Standalone Disc J follows from Sawa–Uchida Theorem 4.8 under parity/quadratic pullback to adjacent quasi-Laguerre.
Characteristic-p U′V−UV′−yUV=−y^p identity used in overlap proof is a hook-partition specialization of known pseudo-Wronskian equivalence and Hermite congruence.

The project applies the classical q→1 Hermite leading part to obtain Disc T_n=(q−1)^(n(n−1)/2)E_n with E_n(1)=product j^j; this proves squarefreeness at primitive p^a-th roots when n<p. The half-degree p^a target for a>1 is not covered.
candidates.model: Primary-source normalization comparisons distinguish fixed-q identities and terminal polynomials from the moving-q local RS theorem.
candidates.proofstatus: Exact reductions documented in saved primary comparison; primary source sections reopened during this catalogue pass.
candidates.noveltystatus: Known/derived from established theory. Must be attributed and unranked.
